I disagree. We are talking about the “Hot” queue which is the default for each sub’s front page. Hot needs to be balanced between timeliness and votes. Currently a 1-year old post with 2 votes will show above a new post with 1 vote, which just doesn’t make sense.

A “Top” queue on the other hand should be based entirely on votes as you said.

Votes should lose weight over time. Here is an example:

Currently:

  1. A post gets 100 upvotes, and reaches the top of the sub.
  2. A week later, a new post appears but only gets 80 votes.
  3. A month later, the newer post has never taken the top spot despite being more current and relevant content.

Ideal:

  1. A post gets 100 upvotes, and reaches the top of the sub.
  2. A week later, a new post appears and gets 80 upvotes. The vote decay of the first post causes the 100 votes to only weigh about 70 votes, while still displaying 100, causing the newer post to rank higher than the older, more upvoted post.
  3. A month later, the newer post (and even newer ones) are appearing at the top of the sub while the older, higher rated post falls quickly away with each day, as the vote decay becomes more and more potent. By a month, 100 votes would be worth barely 5 votes. After 3 months, they're worth nothing.

From a programming standpoint it's merely a matter of calculating the vote total by the number of days since the post was made to get the vote weight, and using vote weight instead of total votes to rank posts. I think new posts should have a vote weight of 1.1 to 1.25 or so. Just to surge them up faster than older posts.
Yep, I agree completely. It will take some tweaking to find out the exact numbers but the current method is not good.

I’m 100% for vote decay. The details can be worked out, but currently a 1-year old post with 2 votes will show above a new post with 1 vote, which just isn’t valid for a “Hot” queue (it would be valid for a “Top” queue).
So the questions are, when should votes start to decay? 24 hours? And what should the rate of decay be? And I think obviously the displayed number does not change.

Oh, and should their be a bottom value? Should that 100 up vote post end up at a value of 50 and stay ahead of anything less? Or could there be some sort of curve so the rate of decay slows over time, but never stops?
/u/Escape had some good ideas covering this. TBH I think this is one of the few things that Reddit does well. That doesn't mean we can't make it better though

Decay the vote weight by 5% per day since post.

Example:

Day Vote Weight Percent of Decay
0 1.00 0%
1 0.95 5%
2 0.85 10%
3 0.72 15%
4 0.58 20%
5 0.43 25%
6 0.30 30%
7 0.19 35%
8 0.11 40%
9 0.06 45%
10 0.03 50%

And so on. I mean that's a pretty rapid decrease, but if we adjust the time frame to what feels natural, that could work. That means by day 7, a post with 100 upvotes only has the weight of 19 effective votes. Any post with 19 real votes or more would beat it in ranking.
